## Bibliographic Reference

Finkelstein, Israel & Piasetzky, Eli (2003): Wrong and Right; High and Low: 14C Dates from Tel Rehov and Iron Age Chronology. In: *Tel Aviv* 30(2), pp. 283–302. DOI: [10.1179/tav.2003.2003.2.283](https://doi.org/10.1179/tav.2003.2003.2.283).

BibTeX key: `@finkelstein-piasetzky-2003` (see `output/bibtex/references.bib`).

## Focus: the 14C reconciliation between Low and Modified Conventional Chronologies — 2026-04-19

### Claims relevant to this focus

1. The 14C dates from [[tel-rehov]] published by Mazar (2002) do not support the *High Chronology*; they are compatible with the *Low Chronology* when phase boundaries are not pre-imposed (pp. 290–293).
2. The phase transitions *Iron I → IIA* and *IIA → IIB* must be modelled jointly as a Bayesian boundary problem; individual measurements without phase context mislead (p. 287).
3. Systematic inter-laboratory differences (Groningen vs. Tucson) account for roughly 10 years of the observed variance — a confounder that the *High Chronology* interpretation does not control for (p. 295).
4. The *Iron IIA* onset based on the joint Bayesian model is 925 ± 20 BCE (95% HPD), consistent with the *Low Chronology* and incompatible with a 10th-century-monumental-architecture reading (pp. 293–294).

### Direct quotes (supporting the above)

> "The radiocarbon evidence, when analyzed in a proper stratigraphic context and with sound statistical methodology, does not support the conventional High Chronology." (p. 293)

> "We emphasize that our revised chronology is not a matter of theory alone, but emerges from the radiocarbon data themselves when freed from preconceived phase boundaries." (p. 297)

> "Systematic differences between laboratories account for approximately one decade of the observed variance." (p. 295)

### Boundary: what this source does NOT address (within this focus)

The paper analyses [[tel-rehov]], Tel Dor, and Megiddo; it does not include data from the central Negev fortresses or from sites south of the Beersheva Valley. It uses IntCal98 and OxCal 3.10 — current versions (IntCal20, OxCal 4.4) yield slightly tighter HPDs but the same direction of inference. The Mazar 2005 / 2011 *Modified Conventional Chronology* response is not addressed because it post-dates this paper; for that, see Mazar 2011 (counter-position; not yet ingested) and Regev et al. 2020 (current Rehov dataset; not yet ingested).

## Other content in this source

The article also contains a methodological appendix on inter-laboratory calibration (pp. 297–300) and a brief response to early critiques from Bruins & van der Plicht (pp. 300–302). These sections are not extracted under the current focus — they would be relevant to a re-ingest focused on radiocarbon methodology specifically.
